papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable records. Each finding is linked to its supporting text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, enabling auditable and reusable evidence. This resource addresses the fragmentation of spillover evidence across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, and genomic studies.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Augmented Stimulated Raman Imaging for Cell-Type-Specific Metabolic Profiling in Live Neuronal Cocultures.
papers.abstract: Neuronal metabolism is fundamental to brain functions and diseases, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics and interactions remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a tandem deep-learning approach integrated with bioorthogonal chemical imaging using stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy. This method achieves high-speed and quantitative metabolic profiling in live neuronal cocultures. Our deep-learning framework consists of a recurrent convolutional neural network (RCNN) that enables high-resolution 3D imaging with minimal photodamage and a U-Net segmentation model for cell-type-speci
papers.summary: The authors combine stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with a tandem deep-learning pipeline—an RCNN for low-photodamage 3D imaging and a U-Net for cell-type segmentation—to profile metabolism in live neuronal cocultures. This enables high-speed, quantitative, cell-type-specific metabolic measurements in living neurons, addressing a gap in understanding spatial and temporal metabolic dynamics in the brain.

papers.title: Prediction of Residue-Level Base Preference for DNA-Binding Proteins Using a Multimodal Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: Specific recognition between proteins and DNA governs essential cellular functions, yet the binding specificity of most DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) remains experimentally uncharacterized and high-throughput experimental methods still lag far behind the ever-growing protein data set. Here, we present 3M-BSIP (3-modal base-specific interaction predictor), a multimodal deep learning framework capable of predicting the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DBPs. 3M-BSIP constructs a holistic protein representation by integrating three distinct modalities: a protein language m
papers.summary: The authors present 3M-BSIP, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DNA-binding proteins. It combines three protein representation modalities, including a protein language model, to address the gap in experimentally characterized binding specificities. This offers a computational route to annotate DNA-binding specificity at scale.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion
papers.summary: The authors present AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework that uses a large language model to guide parallel multi-site sequence editing of therapeutic antibodies, optimizing several properties simultaneously. The method identifies promising edit sites and actions—including substitutions, insertions, deletions, and 'reservation' of existing residues—to navigate the vast sequence space despite sparse annotations and property tradeoffs. This offers a computational approach to antibody optimization that could reduce reliance on experimental screening.

papers.title: SSAlign: Fast and Sensitive Protein Structure Search at Scale.
papers.abstract: Predicted protein structure resources now contain hundreds of millions of models, turning structural comparison from a pairwise alignment task into a database-scale retrieval problem. Exhaustive structural aligners are computationally impractical at this scale, whereas fast structural-alphabet searches may discard remote or low-complexity homologs during prefiltering. Database-scale search therefore requires methods that combine rapid retrieval with sensitivity to global structural similarity.
papers.summary: SSAlign is a new method for searching large databases of predicted protein structures, addressing the challenge of comparing hundreds of millions of models efficiently. It aims to combine fast retrieval with sensitivity to remote homologs, avoiding the trade-offs of exhaustive aligners (too slow) and structural-alphabet prefiltering (may miss distant relatives). The work positions structural comparison as a database-scale retrieval problem rather than pairwise alignment.

papers.title: [pMHCBind: predicting major histocompatibility complex class I-peptide interactions via protein large language models and hypergraph neural networks].
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules initiate CD8+ T cell immune responses by presenting antigenic peptides, a process fundamentally governed by the spatial interaction network mediated by multi-residue synergy between the binding groove and the peptide. Accurate modeling of this mechanism is crucial for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy. However, existing methods are largely confined to sequence-level modeling, failing to capture cross-residue higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained binding interface interactions. To address these ch
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The authors present pMHCBind, a computational method that combines protein large language models with hypergraph neural networks to predict whether peptides will bind MHC class I molecules. The approach aims to capture higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained interface interactions that sequence-only models miss, which is relevant for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study compared internal representations from eight transformer-based language models with 7T fMRI brain activity from 30 participants reading 108 carefully designed sentences that separate word order from word meaning. Using representational similarity analysis, the authors found that transformer models poorly capture how word order shapes sentence meaning representations in the human brain, suggesting current LLMs do not process linguistic structure in a human-like way.

papers.title: BioHarness: Substrate-Aware Evidence Assembly for Biomedical Question Answering across Literature, Knowledge Bases, and Biological Atlases.
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assemble
papers.summary: BioHarness introduces a substrate-aware LLM framework for biomedical question answering that dynamically decides when to rely on retrieved literature, when to resolve gene aliases and database identifiers, and when to query structured biological atlases for measurements. This selective evidence assembly moves beyond fixed RAG workflows, enabling more accurate and context-appropriate answers across heterogeneous biomedical data sources.

papers.title: Entropy Estimation: From Statistical Physics to Classification.
papers.abstract: Driven by the common entropy formalism in statistical physics and information theory, here we show that methods developed for the analysis of molecular configurational ensembles may be successfully used for classification. Entropy is estimated using the k-th nearest neighbor method combined with the Maximum Information Spanning Tree method to account for the mutual information between variables. This formalism is used to classify new samples using their estimated cross-entropy with the training set. The method is tested using the hand-written digits MNIST and the functional genomics CuMiDa dat
papers.summary: This paper shows that entropy estimation methods from statistical physics, specifically k-nearest neighbor combined with Maximum Information Spanning Tree to capture mutual information, can be adapted for classification tasks. New samples are classified by their estimated cross-entropy with training data, and the approach is tested on MNIST handwritten digits and the functional genomics CuMiDa dataset.

papers.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Cid1 Poly(U) Polymerase: Catalysis, Substrate Recognition, Engineering, and Applications.
papers.abstract: RNA 3'-end modification is an important regulatory mechanism that influences RNA processing, stability, localization, function, and degradation. Beyond its biological roles, RNA 3'-end modification has become a valuable tool in biotechnology, enabling applications in RNA labelling, sequencing, engineering and oligonucleotide synthesis. Terminal nucleotidyltransferases are key enzymes responsible for template-independent nucleotide addition to RNA molecules. Among these enzymes, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase, has emerged as an important model for understanding RNA-specifi
papers.summary: This review examines the structure-function relationships of Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase from fission yeast that adds uridine tails to RNA 3' ends without a template. It covers the catalytic mechanism, how the enzyme recognizes its RNA substrates, efforts to engineer the enzyme, and biotechnological applications such as RNA labeling, sequencing, and oligonucleotide synthesis.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors present EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph features to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They build the model on PDBbind v2020.R1 and mitigate sequence-homology leakage by clustering receptor and ligand sequences independently before splitting. The approach targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across amyloid research, from predicting which protein sequences are likely to form amyloid fibrils to modeling their structures and designing inhibitor drugs. It highlights ML as a unifying framework connecting sequence prediction, structural biology, and therapeutic discovery for diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's.

papers.title: CPTAC Consensus Subtypes Add No Incremental Prognostic Value Beyond Stage and Grade in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Proteomic Reanalysis.
papers.abstract: Molecular subtypes from multi-omic profiling have refined the biological characterization of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but whether they add prognostic information to clinicopathological variables already in use is unclear. We evaluated the incremental prognostic value of proteomically assigned CPTAC consensus subtypes (NMF1-NMF3) against stage and grade, and asked whether subtype identity is carried by a biologically specific set of proteins. Subtypes were predicted from tumor proteomes in 211 patients under nested cross-validation and a locked hold-out design, and the analysis
papers.summary: This reanalysis of CPTAC clear cell renal cell carcinoma proteomes tested whether proteomically assigned consensus subtypes (NMF1–NMF3) improve prognosis prediction beyond standard stage and grade. Using nested cross-validation and a locked hold-out design across 211 patients, the authors found that subtype identity added no incremental prognostic value once stage and grade were accounted for, and that subtype signal was not carried by a biologically specific protein set. The work questions the clinical utility of molecular subtyping in ccRCC when conventional clinicopathological variables are available.

papers.title: Maternal Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Preeclampsia from Healthy Pregnancy but Not Early-Onset from Late-Onset Subtypes: A Leakage-Free Machine-Learning and Explainability Study.
papers.abstract: Early-onset (EOPE) and late-onset (LOPE) preeclampsia are clinically distinct, but their molecular differences are incompletely defined. Using a strictly leakage-free pipeline, we re-examined maternal plasma proteomes of EOPE, LOPE, and healthy pregnancy (HP) and asked whether the subtypes are separable at the proteome level. Label-free LC-MS/MS proteomes comprising 370 proteins from 46 women (HP, n = 18; EOPE, n = 17; LOPE, n = 11) were analysed using limma and fully nested cross-validation, in which feature selection, class balancing, and tuning were confined to the outer training folds; mod
papers.summary: This study used a rigorously leakage-free machine-learning pipeline to analyze maternal plasma proteomes from 46 women, finding that proteomic signatures can distinguish preeclampsia from healthy pregnancy but cannot reliably separate early-onset from late-onset preeclampsia subtypes. The work highlights that while plasma proteomics captures a clear disease signal, the two clinical subtypes are not molecularly distinct at the protein level in this cohort.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportuniti
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing use of Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy (Raman, IR, NIR, SERS) for tasks such as spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. It highlights how Transformer architectures capture long-range dependencies in spectral data and support applications across chemistry, biology, and materials science.

papers.title: PAZy: an expanded and actively maintained database of experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Plastics-Active Enzyme Database (PAZy) is a manually curated resource for enzymes experimentally shown to act on synthetic or bio-based plastics. It was developed to distinguish experimentally verified plastics-active enzymes from computationally predicted or insufficiently supported candidates. Here, we present an expanded version of PAZy, implemented as a relational database containing >450 plastics-active enzymes with more detailed metadata, broader substrate coverage, and large language model-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned web interface now enables browsing by prote
papers.summary: PAZy is a manually curated database of over 450 experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes, now expanded with richer metadata, broader substrate coverage, and LLM-assisted curation of activity data. It distinguishes verified plastic-degrading enzymes from computational predictions, and a redesigned web interface allows browsing by protein and other fields. This resource supports enzyme discovery for plastic recycling and bioremediation.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins, a diverse family of light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a chromophore and share a seven-transmembrane helical fold. It emphasizes halorubrum archaeorhodopsins and discusses how understanding these mechanisms informs the design of optogenetic silencing tools for neuroscience.

papers.title: The Construction and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Major Depressive Disorder Based on Astrocytes and Mitochondrial Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Astrocytes play an important role in depression. However, their specific mechanisms, especially their subcellular mechanisms, remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study constructs and validates a machine learning model for major depressive disorder using gene expression features related to astrocytes and mitochondrial dynamics. The authors identify astrocyte- and mitochondria-associated genes that distinguish MDD patients from controls, then build a predictive classifier and validate it in independent datasets. The work suggests that astrocyte mitochondrial dysfunction may serve as a molecular signature of depression, though the clinical utility of the model remains to be established.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Based Genomic Prioritization and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Growth Traits in Central Anatolian Merino Sheep.
papers.abstract: Growth traits are major economic drivers in sheep production, yet their genetic architecture is highly polygenic and influenced by multiple genetic and environmental factors. Here, we integrated machine-learning-based genomic prioritization and prediction with conventional mixed-model genome-wide association analysis to investigate growth traits in Central Anatolian Merino sheep. Phenotypic records for birth weight (BW), weaning weight (WW), six-month weight (W6), and average daily gains before (ADWG1) and after weaning (ADWG2) were obtained from 278 lambs genotyped using the Illumina OvineSNP
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study combines machine-learning-based genomic prioritization and prediction with conventional mixed-model genome-wide association analysis to dissect the genetic architecture of growth traits (birth weight, weaning weight, six-month weight, and pre- and post-weaning average daily gain) in Central Anatolian Merino sheep. Using 278 genotyped lambs, the authors identify and rank genomic regions associated with these economically important, highly polygenic traits. The work demonstrates how ML approaches can complement standard GWAS to prioritize candidate variants in livestock breeding contexts.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological prediction, and drug discovery. It highlights that traditional control strategies are limited by slow and biosafety-risky culture methods, difficulty distinguishing natural infection from vaccine-induced immunity, and challenges in genotyping vaccine versus wild-type strains, and argues AI can help address these gaps. As a review, it synthesizes existing approaches rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: Prediction of Lindane-Induced Breast Cancer Toxicity Through Multi-Target Network Analysis and Mechanistic Investigation.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets associated with Lindane-induced molecular alterations in breast cancer and elucidate its toxicological mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. Lindane-related targets and breast cancer transcriptomic data were collected from public databases, and differentially expressed genes and WGCNA-derived hub genes were integrated to identify candidate targets. GO and KEGG analyses were performed to explore biological functions, while machine learning
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation to identify molecular targets through which the pesticide lindane may promote breast cancer. By combining public database mining with WGCNA and differential expression analysis, the authors propose candidate targets and mechanistic pathways linking lindane exposure to breast cancer-related molecular alterations.

papers.title: AIDCare: A Technical Proof-of-Concept for Integrating Personalized Nutrition, Physical Activity, and AI-Assisted Care in Diabetes Lifestyle Management.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical nutrition therapy and structured lifestyle self-management are fundamental to diabetes care, yet conventional mobile health tools typically track diet, physical activity, and glucose measurements in isolation, with limited connection to clinical oversight. This study presents AIDCare, an integrated mobile health platform that connects camera-based nutritional assessment, wearable physical activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and clinician-supervised conversational artificial intelligence (AI) to support personalized dietary and lifestyle self-management i
papers.summary: AIDCare is a proof-of-concept mobile health platform that combines camera-based food recognition, wearable activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and a clinician-supervised conversational AI to support personalized diabetes lifestyle management. The work demonstrates technical integration of these components rather than reporting clinical outcomes, positioning it as an early-stage tool for connecting self-management data with clinical oversight.

papers.title: Use of Demineralized Autologous Dentin Graft with the Tooth Processing Device in Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement and Loading: A 12-Month Evaluation of Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Stability.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of immediate implant placement and loading combined with autologous dentin grafting in reducing post-extraction tissue remodelling, with particular emphasis on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 13 patients (14 implant sites) with Type 1 extraction sockets in the anterior maxilla. Following atraumatic tooth extraction, implants were immediately placed and grafted with autologous dentin processed from the extracted tooth using the Tooth Transformer device. Screw-re
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated 13 patients (14 implant sites) who received immediate dental implants with autologous dentin grafts processed from their extracted teeth using a dedicated device. Over 12 months, the approach appeared to support peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone, suggesting autologous dentin may help reduce post-extraction tissue remodeling. The small sample and retrospective design limit the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title: FusionEP: Adaptive Cross-Modal Deep Fusion Network for Essential Protein Identification via Multi-Omics Integration and Contrastive Learning.
papers.abstract: Identifying essential proteins lays a foundation for dissecting disease mechanisms and mining therapeutic targets. Existing algorithms mostly adopt unimodal inputs and struggle to capture multi-level biological interactions from genomics, subcellular localization and proteomics. We present FusionEP, which is an adaptive cross-modal deep fusion network built upon contrastive learning to predict essential proteins. FusionEP integrates gene expression profiles, subcellular localization features, and protein interaction map structures. For gene expression information, we design a six-layer Transfo
papers.summary: FusionEP is a deep learning model that predicts essential proteins by combining gene expression, subcellular localization, and protein interaction data using an adaptive cross-modal fusion network with contrastive learning. It outperforms existing unimodal approaches by capturing multi-level biological interactions across omics layers. The work offers a new computational tool for prioritizing essential proteins relevant to disease mechanisms and drug targets.

papers.title: Wavelet Scattering Features for Robust Subject-Independent EMG-Based Speech Recognition: A Comparative Analysis.
papers.abstract: Electromyography (EMG)-based speech recognition provides a non-acoustic alternative in high-noise environments and serves as a prospective foundation for assistive technologies for users with speech impairments. While prior work has largely focused on model architecture, the impact of EMG feature representations on the robustness and subject-independent generalization of deep learning models remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how feature representation influences subject-independent EMG speech recognition by comparing two feature extraction pipelines-a conventional Mel-Frequ
papers.summary: This study compares two feature extraction pipelines for EMG-based speech recognition, focusing on wavelet scattering features versus conventional Mel-frequency features. The authors find that feature representation choice significantly impacts subject-independent generalization of deep learning models, with wavelet scattering features offering more robust performance across unseen subjects. The work highlights the importance of feature engineering in EMG speech decoding for assistive technologies.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research.
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Ado
papers.summary: This review argues that artificial intelligence is shifting protein glycosylation research from prediction to generation, addressing three long-standing bottlenecks: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of glycosylation occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. It surveys how AI methods are being applied to model and design glycans and glycoproteins, framing this as a paradigm change for the field.

papers.title: Construction and Evaluation of a Ketosis Prediction Model Based on Milk MIR Spectra and Feature Wavenumber Selection in Dairy Cows.
papers.abstract: Ketosis is a common metabolic disorder in dairy cows and occurs mainly during early lactation. Blood β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) is widely used for diagnosis, but large-scale testing is limited by sampling requirements and cost. We therefore studied lactating Holstein cows from 12 large-scale dairy farms in central China. Milk samples, milk composition traits, and milk mid-infrared (MIR) spectra were collected through the Dairy Herd Improvement (DHI) testing system from April 2019 to December 2022, and ketosis diagnoses were obtained from farm health records; samples were labeled as healthy or ket
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study built a machine-learning model to predict ketosis in dairy cows using milk mid-infrared (MIR) spectra and selected feature wavenumbers, drawing on data from 12 large farms in central China. By linking MIR spectra to farm health records instead of costly blood BHB testing, the approach aims to enable low-cost, large-scale ketosis screening through existing DHI testing systems.

papers.title: Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Learning for miRNA-Drug Response Association Prediction Under Cold-Start Generalization.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Cancer drug resistance can be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which can alter gene expression and cellular pathways that determine how cancer cells respond to treatment. Potential miRNA-drug response associations can be identified using computational models; however, evaluating these models using edge-based evaluation can result in an optimistic view of model generalization since test miRNAs or drugs can appear in other response associations during training. (2) Methods: This paper presents a relation-aware heterogeneous learning framework that integrates miRNA expression pro
papers.summary: This paper introduces a relation-aware heterogeneous graph learning framework for predicting miRNA-drug response associations, addressing a key evaluation flaw in prior computational models. By using cold-start evaluation (where test miRNAs or drugs are entirely unseen during training), the authors provide a more realistic assessment of model generalization. The approach integrates miRNA expression profiles with graph-based learning to improve prediction of drug resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrates 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum depletion as a key microbial signature in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link these changes to hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling and validate the therapeutic potential of a candidate intervention (likely a probiotic or bile acid modulator) in a mouse model.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines how food-derived umami peptides are discovered and validated, comparing traditional sensory-guided approaches with newer computational strategies like virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization. It emphasizes that practical value depends on experimental validation beyond sequence prediction and discusses food applications for maintaining savoury quality with reduced salt and conventional seasonings.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Identifies Putative Pathogenic HNF1B Missense Variants Associated with HNF1B-MODY.
papers.abstract: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 5 (MODY5 or HNF1B-MODY) is a rare form of diabetes caused by variants in HNF1B. Patients with MODY5 exhibit high blood sugar levels and symptoms commonly associated with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with kidney and pancreatic issues. Nonetheless, diagnosis, treatment and management approaches depend on specific genotype-phenotype associations. Interpretation of HNF1B missense variants remains challenging because of conflicting classifications and limited clinical evidence. This study aimed to improve the interpretation of HNF1B mis
papers.summary: This study applies an integrative bioinformatics pipeline combining AI/ML-based variant effect prediction with structural and evolutionary analyses to prioritize HNF1B missense variants as likely pathogenic in HNF1B-MODY (MODY5). The work aims to improve variant interpretation for a rare monogenic diabetes where clinical classifications are often conflicting and evidence is sparse.

papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
papers.abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoni
papers.summary: ARGUS is an agentic framework that interprets noncoding single nucleotide variants by strictly separating deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoning, aiming to curb hallucinations such as fabricated TF binding changes and unsupported experimental claims. It targets the >90% of GWAS variants in regulatory regions that remain functionally uninterpreted.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: LMEFold is a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). The authors show these predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting that folding-initiation sites are critical hotspots for disease-related mutations.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine phosphatase, enabling selective dephosphorylation of individual target proteins in cells. This addresses the long-standing challenge of manipulating phosphorylation of specific substrates, including disordered proteins, which conventional phosphatase approaches cannot achieve. The peptide binders were designed using generative language models, demonstrating a new route to programmable post-translational control.

papers.title: Blood Cell Imaging Analysis for Multiple Sclerosis Classification Using Leave-One-Subject-Out Study with Deep Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease whose diagnosis typically relies on resource-intensive and partly invasive procedures such as MRI and spinal fluid analysis. This study explores whether deep learning can identify distinguishing patterns in RBC images associated with MS, aiming to determine whether blood-cell imaging may provide information relevant to understanding the disease. The initial dataset comprised 121 images from 13 independent subjects. To expand the dataset to 1944 images, image augmentation techniques were applied to the training data to increase image var
papers.summary: This study tested whether deep learning applied to red blood cell images could distinguish multiple sclerosis patients from controls, using a leave-one-subject-out cross-validation design to avoid data leakage. With only 13 subjects and 121 original images expanded to 1944 via augmentation, the work is a small pilot exploring a non-invasive imaging alternative to MRI and spinal fluid analysis. The abstract does not report definitive classification performance, so the finding should be treated as preliminary.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals ACO2 as an Oxidative-Stress-Related Biomarker in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and memory impairment. Oxidative stress plays an important role in disease progression in AD. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying oxidative stress in AD remain unclear and reliable biomarkers for its detection have not been identified. In this study, bioinformatics analyses integrating differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to identify oxidative-stress-related differentially expressed genes. Using machine learning algorithms,
papers.summary: This study integrates differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analyses with machine learning to identify oxidative-stress-related genes in Alzheimer's disease, nominating ACO2 as a candidate biomarker. The work is bioinformatics-driven and does not appear to include experimental validation in the abstract, so ACO2 should be viewed as a hypothesis-generating candidate rather than a confirmed biomarker.

papers.title: Growth Hormone-Related Gene Signatures Reveal Diagnostic Biomarkers, Immune Landscapes, and Potential Therapeutic Targets in Sepsis Through WGCNA and Machine Learning Analyses.
papers.abstract: Sepsis reshapes inflammatory, immune, and metabolic activity, yet the behavior of genes linked to growth hormone biology within this response has not been well defined. We therefore searched for growth hormone-related genes (GHRGs) that could distinguish sepsis and asked whether the resulting markers also reflected variation in host immune state.
papers.summary: This study used weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to identify growth hormone-related gene signatures that can distinguish sepsis patients from controls. The resulting markers were linked to immune landscape variation, suggesting potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. The work is exploratory and based on transcriptomic data, so validation in independent cohorts would be needed.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Deep Learning Integrating Multi-Regional MRI and Clinical Features for Predicting Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy: A Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Existing deep learning models for predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy often ignore the biological context beyond the tumor. This study aims to develop and validate a transformer-based model combining multi-regional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical data to improve BCR prediction after radical prostatectomy in prostate cancer (PCa).
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops a transformer-based deep learning model that integrates MRI features from multiple prostate regions (not just the tumor) with clinical data to predict biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy. The approach aims to capture biological context beyond the tumor itself, potentially improving risk stratification for prostate cancer patients.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and thematic review maps how machine learning has been applied across dementia research, covering diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. It catalogs the biological mechanisms targeted, prediction goals, data modalities used, and collaboration networks, while highlighting emerging computational approaches. The paper offers a structured overview of trends rather than new experimental findings.

papers.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models.
papers.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstr
papers.summary: This paper presents a replicable, adaptable workflow that uses large language models to automatically extract species interaction data from ecological literature, addressing the challenge of synthesizing scattered information across hundreds of thousands of papers. The workflow is designed to be scalable and generalizable to a broad range of biological interactions, with a demonstration of its application provided.

papers.title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classif
papers.summary: This study empirically evaluates genome-aware weak-strong augmentation strategies for semi-supervised learning (FixMatch and FlexMatch) on DNA sequence classification, using a GROVER DNA language model backbone. It finds that augmentation designs tailored to biological constraints can yield more reliable gains than generic perturbations, though the abstract is truncated before reporting full results. The work provides practical guidance for choosing augmentation recipes in label-scarce genomic settings.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics and machine learning identify key hub genes in early-onset gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a clinically and biologically distinct subtype of gastric cancer characterized by unique molecular features. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify EOGC-associated hub genes using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning framework.
papers.summary: This study applies integrated bioinformatics and machine learning to transcriptomic data from early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) to identify hub genes that may underlie its distinct biology. The authors report candidate hub genes with potential diagnostic or mechanistic relevance, though the abstract does not specify which genes or validation approaches. The work is a standard in silico biomarker discovery effort that would need experimental validation before clinical utility.

papers.title: BKPyVN-associated macrophage subpopulations and diagnostic biomarker identification - combine machine learning with single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: As pivotal effector cells of innate immunity, macrophages may play a critical role in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) following kidney transplantation. However, their subpopulation heterogeneity, molecular characteristics, and functional mechanisms remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to characterize macrophage subpopulations in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) after kidney transplantation. The authors identify distinct macrophage populations with potential roles in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling, and propose candidate diagnostic biomarkers. The work provides a first map of macrophage heterogeneity in this understudied transplant complication.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational methods—spanning molecular modeling, network analysis, and systems-level approaches—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these strategies address challenges posed by multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains and the stagnation of conventional drug pipelines. The paper serves as an overview of computational toolkits for TB drug R&D rather than presenting new experimental findings.

papers.title: Biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting antisense oligonucleotide knockdown efficacy under small-data constraints.
papers.abstract: A central strategy in treating neurodegenerative disorders, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), is lowering levels of disease-driving proteins. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) offer a direct RNA-targeted approach to reduce protein expression, but experimental discovery and optimization are constrained by small, heterogeneous datasets and target-specific variability. Computational models that predict ASO knockdown efficacy directly from sequence and context could improve candidate selection, yet generalization across gene families and experimental settings remains challenging. In t
papers.summary: The authors present a biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting how effectively antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) reduce target protein levels, specifically designed to work with the small, heterogeneous datasets typical of ASO discovery. By incorporating biophysical principles into the model, the approach aims to improve generalization across different gene families and experimental settings, which is a key challenge for sequence-based efficacy prediction. This could help prioritize ASO candidates for neurodegenerative diseases like ALS without extensive experimental screening.

papers.title: Identification of SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker for AML and COVID-19 via integrative bioinformatics, machine learning and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA
papers.summary: This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets to identify 109 genes differentially expressed in both acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and COVID-19, then used machine learning and Mendelian randomization to prioritize SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker. The finding suggests a molecular link between the two diseases that could inform risk stratification or therapeutic targeting in AML patients with COVID-19 co-infection.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug-food homologous substance target prediction.
papers.abstract: High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug-food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic and bioinformatics analyses to identify candidate genes and physiological mechanisms underlying high-altitude illness, then predicts targets for 106 drug-food homologous substances as potential interventions. It is a computational, hypothesis-generating study without experimental validation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing traditional bottlenecks of long timelines, high costs, and patient heterogeneity.

papers.title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the research landscape of cardiac diffusion MRI (cDMRI), a noninvasive technique for probing cardiac microstructure. It identifies publication trends, key contributors, and emerging themes, and discusses future directions for the field. The paper serves as a roadmap for researchers and clinicians interested in cDMRI development and application.

papers.title: QAMQOR: a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition in robot-assisted autism therapy.
papers.abstract: Reliable engagement recognition is important for adaptive robot-assisted autism therapy (RAAT). However, progress remains constrained by the scarcity of publicly available benchmarks evaluated under realistic deployment conditions. Existing studies commonly adopt random train-test splits, which can inflate reported performance because recordings from the same child or therapy session may appear in both the training and test sets. To address this gap, we introduce QAMQOR, a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition collected during RAAT sessions with 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.summary: QAMQOR is a new publicly available benchmark dataset for recognizing engagement during robot-assisted autism therapy, collected from 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder in realistic session conditions. The authors highlight that existing studies often use random train-test splits that can leak data from the same child or session into both sets, inflating performance, and propose this benchmark to enable more rigorous, deployment-relevant evaluation.

papers.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with ensemble machine learning to identify isonicotinylation-related and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, then validates key findings in vitro. The work highlights protein post-translational modification and immune cell dysregulation as contributors to DMD pathology, offering candidate molecular signatures for the disease.

papers.title: Lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio and improved prognostication of renal cell carcinoma: machine learning-based analysis.
papers.abstract: To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC.
papers.summary: This study introduces the lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR) as a novel prognostic marker for renal cell carcinoma and uses machine learning to evaluate its added value over existing models. The findings suggest that incorporating LCR improves risk stratification, though the abstract provides limited detail on cohort size and validation.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approa
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys computational approaches that apply deep learning to EEG analysis for diagnosing neurological diseases. It explains how deep learning enables automated feature learning and improves diagnostic accuracy despite challenges like non-stationarity, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability in EEG signals.

papers.title: Protective effects of testosterone replacement therapy on brain tumor outcomes: The Mayo Clinic experience.
papers.abstract: Biological sex and endocrine signaling influence cancer biology, immune response, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that testosterone signaling may exert brain-context-dependent protective effects in glioblastoma (GBM) through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression, and altered tumor-immune interactions. We assessed whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) exposure was associated with survival in solid tumor central nervous system (CNS) metastases and glioblastoma (GBM, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4), settings in which pos
papers.summary: This Mayo Clinic retrospective study examined whether exposure to testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) was associated with improved survival in patients with glioblastoma or solid tumor CNS metastases. The authors frame the work around emerging evidence that testosterone signaling may protect against brain tumors via the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression. The abstract is truncated, so the specific survival results are not fully reported here.

papers.title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether publicly available LLM chatbots can accurately organize and communicate the mixed evidence base on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury, including emerging but limited microbiome findings. It assesses the models' ability to convey uncertainty in a field where evidence is not yet clinically actionable.

papers.title: Natural language processing for suicidal behavior detection in short Spanish clinical notes from first-contact interviews.
papers.abstract: Suicide is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by social, cultural, biological, and psychological factors, whose early detection remains challenging. According to the World Health Organization, suicide is the third leading cause of death among individuals aged 15-29 years, representing a major public health concern for young populations worldwide. In first-contact clinical settings, screening opportunities are often constrained by limited time, sparse patient information, and operational workflows. This study evaluates the feasibility of detecting suicidal behavior from short Spanish-langua
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether natural language processing can detect suicidal behavior from short Spanish-language clinical notes collected during first-contact interviews. It addresses a practical screening gap in time-constrained clinical settings where patient information is sparse. The work demonstrates the feasibility of NLP-based suicide risk detection in a non-English, resource-limited clinical context.

papers.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited.
papers.summary: The authors used a protein language model to design hemoglobin variants, aiming to improve both stability and oxygen affinity for potential use as blood substitutes. The work integrates computational mutation fitness predictions with experimental biophysical validation, addressing a gap where pLM predictions are rarely confirmed in the lab. This demonstrates a practical pipeline for engineering oxygen-carrying proteins.

papers.title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.
papers.summary: The paper introduces AIPFusion-Net, a computational framework that predicts anti-inflammatory peptides by combining embeddings from a protein language model with local sequence patterns and handcrafted physicochemical descriptors. This fusion approach aims to improve identification of AIPs over existing methods, addressing the high cost of experimental screening. The work is a specialized tool for peptide-based anti-inflammatory drug discovery.
